 ORDER T h e inherent powers of this Court are invoked u/S 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.563/2022 registered at Police Station Maharajpura, District Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 of IPC and Under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and further quashment of other criminal proceedings arising therefrom viz. RCT No. 1880/2023 pending before JMFC, Gwalior, on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

In this petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, the petitioner and respondents No.1 to 3 have filed applications being I.A.Nos. 16454/2023 and 16455/2023 alongwith respective affidavits stating that the dispute between the parties has been resolved and they do not want to pursue the matter any more.

T h e Principal Registrar of this Court has duly verified the parties, contents of the application,
intent and signatures.
Report dated 12.09.2023 is attached and perused.
Compromise has been reached between the parties voluntarily without any threat, inducement and coercion.

In the cases of Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilised in other material cases.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into account the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court, in the opinion of this court, continuance of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.

Consequent upon the above said facts and that the accused petitioner and the complainant/respondents No.1 to 3 have amicably resolved the issue and the offences are being permitted to be compounded with the permission of the Court.
Accordingly, I.As. stand allowed and this Court allows this MCRC with the following direction:-
1 . Crime No.563/2022 registered at Police Station Maharajpura, District Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 of IPC and Under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
is hereby quashed.
2. All the consequential proceedings including RCT No. 1880/2023 pending before JMFC, Gwalior flowing out of the said FIR against the petitioner also stand quashed.
